label.INDPSAFE: Percentage of people feeling very unsafe walking alone in their area after dark

result.label: Indicator - Personal safety
note:
[b]Personal safety[/b] 

[b]How do we measure this?[/b] 
Percentage of people feeling very unsafe walking alone in their area after dark.

[b]Source[/b] 
Northern Ireland Safe Community Telephone Survey, Department of Justice
[url=https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/articles/findings-northern-ireland-safe-community-telephone-survey]https://www.justice-ni.gov.uk/articles/findings-northern-ireland-safe-community-telephone-survey[/url]

[b]Impact of Covid-19[/b] 
There was a change in survey mode from 2020/21 due to the pandemic and the method by which interviews were undertaken changed from face-to-face to telephone. This resulted in a break in the time series. Results for the four latest years, 2020/21 to 2023/24, are not directly comparable with previous sweeps. The change also reduced the sample size for the first two years, particularly in 2020/21.[b] 

Further Information[/b] 
1. The Northern Ireland Safe Community Survey was previously known as the NI Crime Survey. Given the change in survey mode as a result of the pandemic, the survey years from 2020/21 are referenced as the Northern Ireland Safe Community Telephone Survey. 
2. Previously conducted on an ad hoc basis, the survey began operating on a continuous basis in January 2005.
3. Data are available prior to 2006/07, but due to the format used, it is not included here but can be found in the source publication.
4. Results exclude don't knows and refusals.

[b]Age[/b]
5. Missing figures are data which have been suppressed due to small sample sizes (less than 100 respondents).

[b]Marital Status[/b]
6. Figures for 2020/21 are not included as a result of the reduced sample size.
7. All other missing data have been suppressed due to small sample sizes (less than 100 respondents).

[b]Deprivation[/b] 
8. All figures up to and including 2008/09 are based on rank order of super output areas and defined according to the 2005 NI Multiple Deprivation Measure. Figures from 2009/10 to 2017/18 are based on the 2010 NIMDM, while from 2018/19 onwards they are based on the 2017 NIMDM. More information on the NI Multiple Deprivation Measures can be found here: [url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/deprivation]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/deprivation[/url]

[b]Urban Rural[/b]
9. All figures up to and including 2016/17 are based on the Report of the Inter-Departmental Urban-Rural Definition Group; figures from 2017/18 onwards are based on the 2015 NISRA Review of the Statistical Classification and Delineation of Settlements. More information on Urban Rural classifications can be found here: [url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/support/geography/urban-rural-classification]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/support/geography/urban-rural-classification[/url]

[b]Religion[/b]
10. Due to small numbers, figures for 'other' religion and no religion have been combined.

[b]Disability[/b]
11. For this indicator, 'disability' is measured based on the question: 'Do you have any long-standing illness, disability or infirmity? By long-standing, I mean anything that has troubled you over a period of time or that is likely to affect you over a period of time?'.

[b]Dependants[/b]
12. For this indicator, 'has dependants' is measured based on the questions: 'Do you have responsibility for the care of a child?' and 'Do you have responsibility for the care of a person with a disability or a dependant elderly person?'.
